name: Majuro cross-swell observations
summary: Off Majuro, wave buoy measurements were broadly consistent with the boat rocking that Marshallese navigators read as swells bent around islands, though overlapping swells limited proof.
description: Navigator-identified vessel rocking and directional wave measurements were consistent with bent incident swells; multiple wave trains limited field validation.
tier_reason: An explicitly inconclusive specialist wave-field result fits fine detail; do not turn inconclusive into false. This is a scoped consequence judgement, not a reward for documentation or representation.

places.note: Waters west of Majuro and between Majuro and Arno

market.note: Commercial availability is not a milestone of a scientific knowledge result.

date.basis: WAM’s participant interview places buoy deployments during the field year beginning in 2005 and culminating in the 2006 voyage; the research paper also states a June 2005–September 2006 fieldwork interval. Exact deployment days are not given.

events.statement: Navigator-identified vessel rocking and directional wave measurements were consistent with bent incident swells; multiple wave trains limited field validation.
events.place_note: Waters west of Majuro and between Majuro and Arno
events.caveats: The buoy did not resolve claimed reflected signals or dilep. Model agreement at another island is not direct verification of all local cues.

evidence.supports: Experienced rocking, directional components and inconclusive lee-wave validation.
